title: Process Access Request Against The Sensitive Authentication Process
detection_hypothesis: If credential material is harvested from the authentication process, a process access event will record a handle request that includes memory read rights.

field_semantics.TargetImage: Absolute path of the process being accessed.
field_semantics.GrantedAccess: Hexadecimal access mask granted for the process handle.
field_semantics.SourceImage: Absolute path of the process requesting access.

collection_prerequisites: Process access auditing is enabled (Sysmon Event ID 10 or an EDR equivalent).
The sensitive authentication process is included in the monitored target list.
expected_collection_gaps: Process access auditing is often disabled because of its volume.
Kernel-mode access paths are not represented in this event class.
normalization_assumptions: GrantedAccess is a hexadecimal string such as 0x1010.
SourceImage and TargetImage are absolute paths.
ingestion_differences: Some producers emit GrantedAccess as a decimal integer.
CallTrace availability depends on symbol resolution settings.
retention_considerations: Process access telemetry is very high volume; scope filters are required.
expected_volume: Very low once known agents are filtered.
false_positive_strategy: The benign population is a short, enumerable list of security and diagnostic agents. Maintain that list explicitly by source image and review additions, rather than relaxing the access mask selection.
tuning_guidance: Add new agents to the source image filter only after verifying their signature and installation path. Never widen the filter to a directory prefix such as the whole program files tree.
test_strategy: Positive cases request two distinct memory read masks from unmanaged source images. Negative cases cover a low-privilege mask, a different target, and the filtered security agent.
author: Salvatore Mazzaglia
